question: Should exec denylist policy have one canonical persisted owner, or should OpenClaw permanently support the union of `openclaw.json` and `exec-approvals.json`?
rationale: This choice defines a new privileged execution-policy contract, operator upgrade behavior, hot-reload semantics, and future configuration/UI ownership; code review cannot safely infer that product and security direction.

options.title: Use one policy owner
options.body: Keep denylist policy in the exec-approvals owner and remove the parallel `openclaw.json` surface, reducing sources of truth and upgrade ambiguity.

options.title: Accept both surfaces
options.body: Permanently support the union and explicitly document, test, and own migration, hot-reload, protocol, CLI, and UI behavior for both persisted surfaces.

recommendation.title: Use one policy owner
recommendation.body: Keep denylist policy in the exec-approvals owner and remove the parallel `openclaw.json` surface, reducing sources of truth and upgrade ambiguity.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the adjacent delayed exec-approval and macOS commit contract and dominate recent history on the affected paths.
